elements.accessibleMathText: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus 4 a c, all over 2 a
elements.description: The quadratic formula used to solve any second-degree polynomial equation.
stepByStepExplanation: Step 1: Identify the standard quadratic form a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero.
Step 2: Calculate the discriminant under the radical: b squared minus 4 times a times c.
Step 3: If discriminant is positive, calculate two real roots using plus and minus.
Step 4: Divide the combined numerator by 2 times a.

elements.accessibleMathText: 6 molecules of carbon dioxide plus 6 molecules of water react to form 1 molecule of glucose sugar and 6 molecules of oxygen gas
elements.description: Overall chemical reaction equation for oxygenic photosynthesis inside chloroplasts.
stepByStepExplanation: Step 1: Plant leaves absorb 6 molecules of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2).
Step 2: Roots absorb 6 molecules of liquid water (H2O).
Step 3: Sunlight photon energy splits water molecules and fixes carbon inside the stroma.
Step 4: The plant produces 1 stable glucose molecule (C6H12O6) for cellular energy and releases 6 oxygen molecules (O2) into the atmosphere.

variables.meaning: Oxygen gas released into the atmosphere

elements.rawText: Chlorophyll Light Absorption Spectrum vs Wavelength (nm)
elements.accessibleMathText: A line graph showing light absorption versus wavelength from 400 to 700 nanometers. Chlorophyll absorbs strongly in blue and red light, but reflects green light.
elements.description: Absorption spectrum graph demonstrating how chlorophyll pigments absorb light wavelengths.
stepByStepExplanation: Step 1: The horizontal axis measures light wavelength in nanometers from 400 (violet) to 700 (red).
Step 2: The vertical axis measures percentage of solar photon absorption.
Step 3: A sharp blue peak appears at 430 nanometers.
Step 4: Absorption drops to near zero in the green band (500–550 nm), which is reflected back to our eyes.
Step 5: A second high peak appears at 660 nanometers in the red spectrum.
